compiled_state.title: [sub-agent dispatch]: isolation:worktree creates worktree from origin/main instead of session HEAD -> sub-agent does not see in-flight session work
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Reproduction

1. Orchestrator session is on branch `session-<timestamp>` ahead of `main` with N commits (in-flight work — predecessor RED tests, freshly extracted libraries, new modules).
2. Orchestrator dispatches a sub-agent with `isolation: "worktree"`.
3. The agent runtime creates the worktree branched from `origin/main` (NOT from the session HEAD).
4. Sub-agent's worktree therefore does not contain the in-flight session work.
5. Sub-agent's task may depend on that work (e.g., S7.T6 implementing aggregator.py needs the S7.T5 RED test file that was just committed on the session branch).
6. Sub-agent either fails to find the dependency OR duplicates it (re-creating files from scratch), causing harvest-time conflicts.

## Expected

Worktree should branch from the session HEAD (orchestrator's current commit) so the sub-agent sees all in-flight work. OR: dispatch should provide a clear documented contract that worktrees are based on main and require explicit sync.

## Actual

Worktrees consistently branch from origin/main. Sub-agents must explicitly `git fetch origin <session-branch> && git reset --hard origin/<session-branch>` at start of work. The orchestrator must include this instruction in every dispatch prompt. Easy to forget; cost is significant when forgotten.

## Evidence

- Memory file feedback_worktree_subagent_pitfalls.md (#1 Base-branch drift, 2026-05-02): documents the recurring pattern across multiple sprints.
- Epic f691-681e (PR #245), S7.T6 sub-agent (agent-a55d462efcdf83a1a):
  - Worktree base commit: `83870f08ae` (= origin/main HEAD at time of dispatch)
  - Session HEAD at dispatch: `97c922c11a` (had 22 commits ahead of main including S7.T5 RED test file)
  - Sub-agent reported: "test_dso_ci_review_aggregator.py — copied from session branch (the RED test file that T5 already committed)". The agent had to COPY the RED test file from the session worktree because its own worktree was based on main and didn't have the file.
- This pattern was observed across 6+ dispatches this session; the explicit `git fetch origin <session-branch> && git reset --hard origin/<session-branch>` instruction had to be added to every dispatch prompt as a workaround.

## Cost

Per dispatch: ~5 extra lines of prompt boilerplate. Per session: when the instruction is forgotten or the sync fails silently, recovery costs 15+ min per affected sub-agent.

## Proposed fix

Option A (preferred): worktree-dispatch.md prompt template inserts the sync step automatically when SESSION_BRANCH != main. Orchestrators always pass SESSION_BRANCH + SESSION_HEAD; the template handles the sync.

Option B: the Agent tool runtime (or worktree-session-head-sync.sh) creates worktrees branched from the orchestrator's HEAD, not from origin/main. Removes the need for any prompt-level workaround.

Option C: document the contract publicly so it stops being a hidden footgun. (Acceptable interim — but the cost of forgotten sync is real.)

- Bug filed this session: <new-id> (worktree-isolation-leakage) — same root area, different failure mode
